subject: Biotechnology
title: Cancer Vaccines
description: A quick, practical guide to Cancer Vaccines.

hook.text: Can you vaccinate against cancer? Neoantigen vaccines teach your immune system to hunt your specific tumor.

buildup.text: Sequence the tumor's DNA, find mutations unique to it, and design an mRNA vaccine encoding those neoantigens.

discovery.text: Moderna's personalized cancer vaccine mRNA-4157 plus Keytruda cut melanoma recurrence by 44% in a Phase 2 trial.

twist.text: Every patient gets a different vaccine — manufacturing a unique drug per person upends traditional pharma economics.

climax.text: HPV vaccines prevent cervical cancer by stopping the virus — Gardasil prevents over 90% of HPV-related cancers.

punchline.text: Prevent or attack — cancer vaccines work both ways.

quiz.question: How are personalized cancer vaccines designed?
options: They use a standard protein found in all cancers
Tumor DNA is sequenced to find unique mutations, then a vaccine encoding those neoantigens is made
They are made from weakened cancer cells injected back into the patient
